clauses.reason: The approving paragraph of Executive Order 6641 reads: "Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do approve the report and recommendations, and adopt the findings of the Administrator and do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved, subject to the following conditions:". It approves the code of the Scrap Iron, Nonferrous Scrap Metals and Waste Materials Trade, subject to the one condition set out in the following paragraph (its own clause). The approval states no period, until-date or provisional approval; the 1944 WPA list describes it as "conditionally approved", which refers to that condition. The approval was code-dependent: under section 3(b) of the Act the approved provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under section 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under section 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor, so the approval operated only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval, so the approval ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end date: section 1 of the same resolution replaced the original two-year expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not as an end date.

The condition paragraph of Executive Order 6641 reads: "The Code Authority for the "Waste Paper Trade" and/or the Administration Member on said Code Authority shall report to the Administrator not later than sixty (60) days after the effective date hereof, whether or not a supplementary Code is necessary or desirable for the "Waste Paper Trade" and recommend all necessary provisions for such supplementary code. Such recommendations when approved by the Administrator after such notice and hearing as he may deem proper shall have the same force and effect as other provisions of this Code.". It directs the Code Authority for the Waste Paper Trade (and the Administration Member on it) to report within sixty days after the order's effective date whether a supplementary code is needed, and gives recommendations later approved by the Administrator the force of provisions of the code. The sixty-day period is a deadline for the report, not an end of the direction: the direction is addressed to a body that exists only under the code, no held record shows the report made or when, and so the deadline supplies no end and the direction is not recorded as exhausted. The direction and the force given to approved recommendations depend on the approved code (section 3(a) allows the President to impose conditions of approval, including reports). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the provisions delegating power to approve codes and providing for their enforcement, effective on its approval, June 14, 1935, so the direction and the supplementary-code mechanism ceased to operate on that date. No held record shows a supplementary Waste Paper code approved. June 16, 1935 is not an end date: section 1 of the same resolution replaced the original two-year expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory has one clause for the whole paragraph. The paragraph contains two commands: the approval of the code, and the condition directing the Code Authority for the Waste Paper Trade to report on a supplementary code. They have different subjects and are separated so that each gets its own end reasoning.

Second command of the same order: the condition directing the Code Authority for the Waste Paper Trade to report within sixty days whether a supplementary code is needed. Separated from the approval as its own clause.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6641 (March 12, 1934) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Scrap Iron, Nonferrous Scrap Metals and Waste Materials Trade under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; Common Crawl capture 2025-10-10T13:21:51Z); the standing note applies: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order has two commands: the approval, and the condition directing the Waste Paper Trade Code Authority to report on a supplementary code within sixty days. Because each command is dependent on the code and no held record shows an earlier end, the first end is the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, effective June 14, 1935. Schechter, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; that is recorded as a validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no approval. The antitrust-exemption proviso of the resolution is not settled by the held text for past action; whatever survives is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
